propositions: Six proposed deterministic clarity criteria were tested against 574 closed tickets with signed attestation; all six have historical counterexamples in closed, accepted tickets that would be rejected by literal implementation of the rule.

Required nonempty canonical section headings (Approach, Scope) are insufficient validity gates because semantic aliases, compact inline plans, and content-bearing alternate headings carry the same executable information.
Placeholder-lexicon detectors produce false positives on mechanically decidable conditionals and bounded scope statements expressed in AC rather than dedicated Scope sections.

Per-AC explicit proof-coverage markers (verified by, verify with) are not necessary gates because precise behavioral oracles exist without sentinel phrases and historical tickets with zero markers have passing reviews.

Edit-set and file_impact requirements are inapplicable to analysis, probe, and operational tickets with explicit no-edit output contracts; ticket 0730 demonstrates valid probe work with empty file_impact and durable comment-based output.
Conjunction-count and testing-shape heuristics cannot distinguish coherent cross-surface matrices from vague stubs and should remain advisory signals rather than hard validity rules.
